screening_decisions.reason: Cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating multiple biomarkers (HE4, CA125, ROMA, RMI) in 1218 patients with pelvic masses. Uses histological diagnosis as reference standard. Directly addresses the review question of test combinations for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Prospective cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study of 108 women with pelvic masses. Evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA for differentiating endometriosis from carcinoma. Uses pathological results as reference standard. Meets selection criteria.

Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study of 278 patients with adnexal masses. Evaluates ADNEX model (multivariable ultrasound model) with and without CA125. Uses histopathological diagnosis as reference standard. Meets selection criteria for validating multivariable models.

Retrospective case note audit examining CA125 usage patterns and appropriateness in clinical practice, NOT a diagnostic test accuracy study. Does not evaluate test accuracy in women with pelvic masses suspicious for ovarian cancer. Does not meet selection criteria.

Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study validating ADNEX model and comparing with other prediction models (LR2, RMI) in 326 patients with adnexal masses. Uses pathology as reference standard. Addresses test combinations and model validation.

Systematic review and meta-analysis, NOT a primary diagnostic test accuracy study. The review protocol specifies inclusion of primary studies (cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy studies, randomized trials, model validation studies), not secondary research.

Diagnostic accuracy study of 408 patients with adnexal masses. Evaluates RMI 1-4 using ultrasound, menopausal status, and CA125. Uses histopathologic results as endpoint. Directly addresses the review's focus on test combinations including menopausal status.

Prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy trial of 2481 women. Compares HE4, CA125, and ROMA diagnostic accuracy by menopausal status and cancer stage. Meets criteria for comparing two or more tests.

Diagnostic accuracy study comparing HE4, CA125, and ROMA in patients with benign and malignant gynecological diseases including 111 ovarian cancer cases. Evaluates test performance with ROC analysis. Meets selection criteria.

Systematic review about symptoms associated with ovarian cancer diagnosis, NOT a diagnostic test accuracy study. Does not evaluate menopausal status, ultrasound, or biomarker tests. Does not meet selection criteria.
Systematic review and meta-analysis, NOT a primary diagnostic test accuracy study. The review protocol specifies inclusion of primary studies only.
Epidemiological/statistical report on global cancer burden. Does not evaluate diagnostic test accuracy for ovarian cancer. Does not meet selection criteria.

Prospective multicentre diagnostic study of 5909 women with ovarian masses across 24 ultrasound centres in 10 countries. Validates ADNEX model (multivariable model with clinical and ultrasound predictors) with histological classification as outcome. Directly addresses the review question.

Retrospective study of 247 women with adnexal neoplasia. Compares discriminative value of CA-125, HE4, RMI-II, and ROMA. Uses histological diagnosis. Meets selection criteria for comparing multiple tests.

Prospective case-control study of 159 women with adnexal masses. Evaluates HE4 and CA125 alone and in combination. Uses ROMA for risk categorization. Meets selection criteria for evaluating test combinations.

Diagnostic accuracy study of 419 women including 114 EOC cases. Evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA by menopausal status. Uses preoperative serum samples with pathology reference. Meets selection criteria.

Prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study of 2403 patients with adnexal masses. Compares IOTA strategies, RMI, and ultrasound-based models. Uses histology as reference standard. Directly addresses diagnostic test accuracy for ovarian cancer.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating RMI which combines CA125, ultrasound score, and menopausal status in 143 patients with pelvic masses. Directly addresses the review's focus on combinations including menopausal status. Uses histological confirmation.

Basic science/biomarker expression study using immunohistochemistry on tissue samples. Does not evaluate diagnostic test accuracy in women with pelvic masses. Does not meet selection criteria for diagnostic accuracy studies.

Diagnostic accuracy study comparing CA125, HE4, and ROMA in 373 patients divided by menopausal status. Uses ROC curve analysis for performance comparison. Meets selection criteria for comparing multiple tests.
Prospective study of 394 women with cystic ovarian masses. Evaluates HE4 and CA-125 biomarkers with ROMA algorithm. Uses histological classification as reference. Meets selection criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study of 96 patients with benign diseases, 47 with ovarian cancer, and 106 healthy women. Compares CA125, HE4, and ROMA performance. Meets selection criteria for evaluating diagnostic tests.

Prospective validation study of 1938 women with adnexal masses. Evaluates simple ultrasound rules with histological classification as reference standard. Meets selection criteria for diagnostic test accuracy studies.

Cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study evaluating ROMA (combination of HE4 and CA125) in 260 postmenopausal women with ovarian masses. Histopathological verification used as reference standard. Directly meets selection criteria for women with pelvic masses suspicious for OC.
Epidemiological projection study modeling cancer incidence and mortality trends. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study. Does not evaluate diagnostic tests in women with pelvic masses.
Qualitative study exploring patient experiences with diagnosis. No diagnostic test accuracy evaluation. Does not assess diagnostic tests or their accuracy.
Review article on ovarian cancer biology and mouse models. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study. Does not evaluate diagnostic tests in clinical practice.

Nested case-control study of prediagnostic biomarkers in general population cohort (Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial). Not women with pelvic masses suspicious for OC. Wrong population for this review.
Methodological paper describing quality assessment tool for diagnostic accuracy studies. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study itself.

Validation study of ROMA algorithm (CA125, HE4, and menopausal status) in 207 women with pelvic mass. Histologic diagnosis used as reference standard. Meets selection criteria for test validation in women with pelvic masses.
Literature review on CA125 antigen. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not provide new diagnostic accuracy data.
Review proposing model of ovarian cancer pathogenesis. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study. No evaluation of diagnostic tests.
Critical review of proteomic technologies for ovarian cancer. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study evaluating specific tests in clinical practice.
Diagnostic accuracy study validating RMI in 540 women with adnexal tumors. Expert ultrasound and histopathological findings used as reference. Meets selection criteria for women with pelvic masses.
Diagnostic accuracy study of ROMA in 443 patients with pelvic mass. Biopsy or clinical follow-up used as reference standard. Evaluates biomarker combination test. Meets selection criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating expert sonography, CA-125, RMI and their combinations in 1362 patients with adnexal masses. Surgical outcomes as reference. Meets selection criteria for test combinations.

Prospective multicenter cross-sectional study validating IOTA ultrasound strategy in 1165 women with adnexal masses. Histological diagnosis as reference standard. Evaluates ultrasound-based diagnostic approach. Meets selection criteria.
Methodological paper on publication bias testing in meta-analyses of diagnostic accuracy. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA in 756 patients with pelvic masses. ROC analysis with histological confirmation. Evaluates biomarker combinations. Meets selection criteria.

External validation study of IOTA ADNEX model in 327 patients with adnexal masses from two centers. Surgical/histological outcomes as reference standard. Meets selection criteria for multivariable model validation.

Cohort study evaluating implementation of symptom-triggered testing guidelines. Focuses on referral pathways and stage shift, not diagnostic test accuracy in women with pelvic masses. Wrong study design.

Prospective multicenter study validating HE4 and CA125 algorithm in 531 women with pelvic masses. Surgical outcomes as reference standard. Evaluates multivariable model for EOC risk. Meets selection criteria.
Clinical practice guideline document for evaluation and management of adnexal masses. Not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not provide new diagnostic accuracy data.
Molecular genetics study investigating ARID1A mutations in ovarian carcinomas. Not a diagnostic test accuracy study. No evaluation of diagnostic tests in women with pelvic masses.

Abstract appears incomplete. Title suggests comparison of HE4 with other markers, but abstract is truncated and does not describe a diagnostic accuracy study with reference standard. Cannot confirm it meets selection criteria.

Prospective multicenter study evaluating HE4 and ROMA in 414 women with adnexal masses from six Asian countries. Surgical outcomes as reference standard. Evaluates biomarker combinations. Meets selection criteria.

This is an epidemiological incidence study examining trends in borderline tumors and ovarian cancer over time. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests, multivariable models, or test combinations for ovarian cancer diagnosis in women with pelvic masses. No diagnostic accuracy measures are reported.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of existing literature, not a primary cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study. The protocol specifies inclusion of primary diagnostic test accuracy studies, not secondary research syntheses.

Prospective trial evaluating the ROMA index (multivariable model combining CA125 and HE4) for predicting malignancy in women with adnexal masses. Uses pathological results as reference standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study validating a multivariable model.

Prospective multicentre cross-sectional study evaluating IOTA prediction models (LR2), ultrasound Simple Rules, and RMI for preoperative characterization of adnexal masses. Uses histological diagnosis as reference standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.

This is a meta-analysis of 32 studies, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study. The protocol requires primary cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy studies or validation studies, not systematic reviews or meta-analyses.

Prospective cross-sectional study evaluating CA-125, HE4, ROMA, and RMI in women with ovarian lesions. Uses histopathological diagnosis as gold standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.

Multicenter study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA in patients with suspicious pelvic masses requiring surgery. Uses histological confirmation as reference standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.

This is a methodological paper describing statistical approaches for meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy studies. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests for ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses.
This is a methodological simulation study about meta-analysis methods for diagnostic test accuracy. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests for ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses.

This is a genetic study examining inherited mutations in women already diagnosed with ovarian/peritoneal/fallopian tube carcinoma. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests for women with pelvic masses suspicious for ovarian cancer.

This is a review article covering prevalence, etiology, risk factors, diagnosis, and treatment of ovarian cancer. It is not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating tests in women with pelvic masses.

Prospective multicenter blinded clinical trial evaluating ROMA algorithm in women presenting with pelvic/adnexal masses. Uses histological diagnosis as reference standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.

Prospective study of 100 women with pelvic masses evaluating four RMI versions (RMI 1-4) for detecting malignant ovarian tumors. Uses surgical exploration as reference standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.
Study evaluating RMI, CA-125, and inflammatory markers in postmenopausal women with adnexal masses. Uses surgery as reference standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.
Study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA for differentiating benign from malignant ovarian diseases. Uses ROC analysis for diagnostic performance. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.

This is a case-control study examining symptoms of ovarian cancer in primary care records. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests in women with pelvic masses. Population and study design do not match protocol criteria.

Prospective validation study of ROMA algorithm in women with pelvic masses scheduled for surgery. Evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA. Uses histological diagnosis as reference standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of 96 validation studies, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study. The protocol requires primary studies, not secondary research syntheses.

Study evaluating CA125, HE4, ROMA, and RMI for classifying ovarian masses. Uses ROC curves for diagnostic performance assessment. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.
This is a clinical practice guideline/statement about genetic risk assessment for hereditary cancer syndromes. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests for ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses.
Cross-sectional study evaluating CA-125, HE4, and ROMA in women with ovarian masses. Uses postoperative histopathology as reference standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.
Study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA2 index in postmenopausal women with ovarian cancer vs benign tumors. All diagnoses histologically verified. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.

Study evaluating 2D ultrasound, CA125, RMI, IOTA simple rules, LR2, and 3DPD ultrasound in postmenopausal women with ovarian tumors. Uses histopathological results as reference standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study.

This is a systematic review/meta-analysis of 16 articles, not a primary cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study. The protocol requires primary studies evaluating tests, not secondary syntheses of existing literature.

This is a diagnostic study enrolling 129 patients with pelvic masses suspected of ovarian origin. It evaluates HE4, CA-125, and ROMA (combination) with sensitivity/specificity/AUC analysis. Reference standard appears to be surgery/biopsy. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.

Prospective study of 50 women with complex pelvic masses evaluating HE4, CA125, ROMA, and RMI. Uses histological diagnosis as reference standard. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.

This is a methodology paper describing the PROBAST tool for assessing risk of bias in prediction model studies. It is not a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating tests for ovarian cancer diagnosis in women with pelvic masses.

Study of 104 women with pelvic mass evaluating ROMA (combination of HE4 and CA125) with histological reference standard. Provides diagnostic accuracy measures (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) for pre- and postmenopausal women. Meets criteria for diagnostic test accuracy study validating a multivariable model.

This study examines routes to cancer diagnosis using administrative data across all cancer types in England. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests for ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses. Wrong population and outcome.
This is a methodological paper discussing statistical approaches for meta-analysis of diagnostic studies. It is not a primary diagnostic accuracy study evaluating tests for ovarian cancer.

Prospective population-based study of 901 women with pelvic masses evaluating RMI, ROMA, CA125, and HE4. Includes pre- and postmenopausal women with reference standard. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.
This is a software user guide for meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy studies. It is not a primary diagnostic accuracy study evaluating tests for ovarian cancer diagnosis.
This is a meta-analysis of 11 studies comparing ROMA, HE4, and CA125. It is a systematic review, not a primary cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study as required by the protocol.

Multicenter study of 2445 patients with adnexal masses evaluating IOTA models (LR1, LR2), IOTA simple rules, and RMI. Uses histological diagnosis as reference standard. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating multivariable models.

Subset analysis of 229 premenopausal patients with adnexal masses evaluating HE4 and CA-125 for EOC detection. Provides sensitivity/specificity measures. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study in premenopausal women.

This study focuses on prediction and therapy-monitoring/prognosis in 123 ovarian cancer patients, not diagnostic accuracy in women with pelvic masses suspicious for OC. The outcome is prognosis/therapy response, not initial diagnosis.
This study examines 1042 women with benign gynecological disorders only, not women with pelvic masses suspicious for ovarian cancer. It does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy for OC diagnosis.
This is a review article discussing biomarkers for ovarian cancer screening, diagnosis, and monitoring. It is not a primary diagnostic accuracy study evaluating tests in women with pelvic masses.

This is a laboratory method development study creating an HE4 ELISA assay. While it includes blinded studies on postmenopausal patients, it is primarily a biomarker development paper, not a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating tests in clinical practice for women with pelvic masses.
This is a systematic review of 109 accuracy studies on prediction models. It is a secondary synthesis, not a primary cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study as required by the protocol.

This systematic review evaluates sentinel node biopsy for endometrial (womb) cancer, not ovarian cancer. Wrong cancer type and wrong clinical question (lymph node staging vs primary diagnosis of pelvic mass).
This is a meta-analysis of studies using IOTA simple rules, including a validation study. As a meta-analysis, it is a secondary synthesis rather than a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

Diagnostic performance study of 762 patients with benign disease and 70 with ovarian cancer evaluating CA125, HE4, and ROMA. Provides sensitivity/specificity/AUC for pre- and postmenopausal women. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study.

This is a review article comparing diagnostic indices. It summarizes existing evidence rather than presenting primary diagnostic accuracy data from a cross-sectional study of women with pelvic masses.

Multicenter clinical trial of 638 women with ovarian cyst or pelvic tumor evaluating HE4, CA125, ROMA, and RMI. Uses final pathology report as reference standard. Includes pre- and postmenopausal women. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study comparing multiple tests.

Study of 353 patients with adnexal masses evaluating ADNEX model vs subjective assessment. Uses histological diagnosis as reference standard. Includes pre- and postmenopausal women. Meets criteria for cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study validating a multivariable model.
